blogs.title: Mining 120B Math Tokens from the Open Web: A Hands‑On Guide to Domain Data at Scale
blogs.description: Walk through the iterative pipeline used to build the DeepSeekMath corpus from Common Crawl. Covers fastText-based classification, domain discovery, deduplication, multilingual coverage, and benchmark decontamination so practitioners can adapt the recipe to other domains like coding or finance.

blogs.title: GRPO Explained: Reinforcement Learning for LLMs Without a Critic
blogs.description: An accessible deep dive into Group Relative Policy Optimization, a PPO variant that replaces the critic with group-relative baselines. Learn how GRPO reduces memory, stabilizes training with KL regularization, and boosts mathematical reasoning, plus when to prefer outcome vs process supervision.

blogs.title: Does Code Training Improve Reasoning? What We Learned from DeepSeekMath
blogs.description: A practitioner-focused analysis of why starting from a code-pretrained base helps math reasoning both with and without tools. Includes practical training recipes (two-stage vs mixed), pitfalls like catastrophic forgetting, and how to balance code and math data on a budget.

blogs.title: Small Models, Big Math: How a 7B LLM Reached Competition‑Level Accuracy
blogs.description: A story for tech enthusiasts about how a 7B open model can approach GPT-4-class math performance without external tools. Breaks down the ingredients: high-quality web data, instruction tuning with CoT and PoT, and lightweight RL—plus what these results mean for democratizing advanced reasoning.

blogs.title: From SFT to RL: A Practical Map of Modern LLM Training (RFT, DPO, PPO, GRPO)
blogs.description: Demystify today’s training methods using a unified paradigm. Compare data sources (online vs offline), reward signals (rule vs model), and gradient coefficients to help ML engineers choose the right technique for their constraints and goals.

blogs.title: Building a Multilingual Math LLM: Lessons on Cross‑Lingual Reasoning
blogs.description: What it takes to make an LLM excel at math in both English and Chinese. Discusses multilingual data curation, transfer effects across languages, and why English-only corpora can underperform on non-English benchmarks.

blogs.title: Why ArXiv Alone Won’t Make Your LLM a Math Genius
blogs.description: A counterintuitive look at why arXiv-heavy pretraining may not improve math reasoning. Reviews controlled experiments, caveats, and practical guidance on when and how to combine scholarly papers with curated web data.

blogs.title: Tool‑Integrated Reasoning 101: Teaching LLMs to Use Python for Math
blogs.description: A starter guide for students and practitioners on program-of-thought prompting. Shows how to get LLMs to solve problems with Python and libraries like sympy, plus tips to evaluate and debug tool-augmented solutions.

blogs.title: Sampling for Stronger Reasoning: Self‑Consistency, Maj@K, and Decoding Tricks
blogs.description: A practical explainer of why multiple sampled chains can dramatically boost correctness in math tasks. Covers self-consistency, Maj@K vs Pass@K, and cost/latency trade-offs so teams can tune decoding strategies effectively.

blogs.title: Data Decontamination in the Age of Benchmarks: How to Stay Honest and Still Scale
blogs.description: Concrete techniques to avoid test leakage while mining the web at scale. Explains n-gram filtering, dedup strategies, and how to audit pipelines so your benchmark scores are trustworthy.

blogs.title: Formal Math Meets LLMs: Auto‑Formalization with Isabelle and miniF2F
blogs.description: An intro to formal theorem proving for LLM-curious readers. Explains informal-to-formal translation, proof sketches, and how automated tools like Sledgehammer fit into an LLM-assisted proving workflow.

blogs.title: What’s Next for RL in Reasoning LLMs: Process Rewards, Iteration, and Weak‑to‑Strong
blogs.description: Forward-looking ideas for researchers and advanced practitioners. Discusses iterative RL with replay, process vs outcome rewards, improving reward model generalization and uncertainty, and weak-to-strong alignment to handle noisy supervision.
